sheet-1-1.description: The main map of Sheet 1 shows North Main Street in Stewartsville, Greenwich Township, from the dry bed of the former Morris Canal at the top of the sheet south to the Presbyterian Church, where Sheet 2 continues. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper right. The street is drawn 20 feet wide at the canal and 40 feet wide further south, with paired old and new house numbers along both frontages. The northern half is open country: scattered frame dwellings and barns, and the E. C. Brill stock farm with its stables, pig house, wagon houses, ice and wash houses and farm implement sheds, crossed by an unnamed brook flowing south. Two lanes leave North Main Street, School House Lane to the west and Temple Lane to the east, both marked as arbitrary. South of School House Lane the street is built up on narrow, deep lots with frame dwellings and outbuildings, the public school (brick, steam heat, electric light), the First Lutheran Church with its belfry, hitching sheds, and at the foot of the sheet the Presbyterian Church. Melick Brook runs south behind the east-side lots. The upper right of the sheet holds the title cartouche, legend, location map, specials index and a key map at 1000 feet to an inch; these are outside this part, as is the inset of East Washington Street at the lower right. The scale bar and a compass rose are drawn at the lower left and left margin.
notes: North Main is today's North Main Street; School House Lane and Temple Lane have no named counterpart in OpenStreetMap.
The Morris Canal is shown as a dry bed ('Dry Bed of Former Morris Canal').
The school is lettered 'Puplic School' on the sheet.
No modern street junction lies on this part; it is placed from one point carried from sheet 3 (the canal crossing) and three building corners carried from sheet 2.

Scale 100 ft. Title cartouche, key, location map, specials index and a key map at 1000 ft (top right, not configured). Part 1: North Main Street from the dry bed of the former Morris Canal south to the Presbyterian Church, with School House Lane and Temple Lane (no modern names) and the E. C. Brill stock farm; no modern junction drawn, placed from points carried from sheets 3 and 2. Part 2 (inset): East Washington Street east end with the Lane (Watertower Road) and Road (Willow Grove Road, modern junction realigned, not used).

sheet-1-2.description: This inset at the lower right of Sheet 1 shows the east end of East Washington Street, continuing the street from the right edge of Sheet 2. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing to the upper right. The street runs across the inset from the left, where an 18 foot lane leaves it, to a road at the right edge, with house numbers 101 to 113 on the north side and 114 to 126 on the south. The north side (block 217) is almost empty, with a single dwelling and a shed at the west end. The south side (block 218) is divided into deep lots, most with a small frame dwelling and sheds or auto houses at the rear along an unnamed back lane that runs parallel to the street. A 40 foot lane runs south from East Washington Street in the middle of the inset and curves into the back lane; east of it are a few more lots and a transforming station near the road. The rest of the inset is blank paper marked no exposure.
notes: East Washington is today's Washington Street; the Lane is Watertower Road, which still loops behind the lots as the drawn back lane does.
The Road at the right edge is Willow Grove Road; its modern junction with Washington Street lies about 15 m east of the drawn one and was not used.
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Washington Street / Watertower Road) with the atlas scale and a north of 44 degrees; low confidence.

sheet-2-1.description: The main map of Sheet 2 shows the centre of Stewartsville at the crossing of North and South Main Street with Greenwich or West Washington Street and East Washington Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, twice the scale of the other sheets, and turned so that north points to the upper right. The crossing is a wide open square. Around it are the commercial buildings of the village: stores and dwellings of frame and stone, a brick and stone block, the post office with the I.O.O.F. hall upstairs, and a garage with concrete floor for 28 cars on East Washington Street. Mellick's Brook runs south across the east of the sheet under a concrete and iron bridge on East Washington Street, and a second brook runs south across the west, bridged on West Washington Street and at a driveway. Along South Main Street are dwellings, an auto implement store and auto storage, an undertaker's shop and barns. West of the brook are Henry Kinkel and Son's stone crushing works with an engine and machine shop marked not running, and the limestone quarry with an incline track. A lane runs south from East Washington Street on the east side of the sheet, beside a vacant field. The lower right corner holds a separate inset of South Main Street further south.
notes: Greenwich or West Washington is today's Greenwich Street; East Washington is Washington Street.
The Driveway west of South Main is today's Fulmer Street (about 4 m from the fit).
Scale bar gives about 8.05 px/ft, close to twice the 100 ft sheets' 4.15 px/ft used for the fit.
Placed from one hand-picked point at the central crossing with the atlas scale and a north of 44 degrees (the sheet's own north arrow); low to medium confidence.

Scale 50 ft (bar). Part 1: the village centre, North and South Main Street at Greenwich or W. Washington and E. Washington Street, Post Office, Kinkel limestone quarry; Driveway = modern Fulmer Street. Part 2 (inset, lower right): South Main Street continued south to the Lane, same orientation and scale as part 1, placed from points carried from part 1.

sheet-2-2.description: This inset at the lower right of Sheet 2 continues South Main Street south of the main map, at the same scale of 50 feet to an inch and the same orientation, with north to the upper right. South Main Street runs down the inset from the top, where the brick and frame dwelling at the edge of the main map is drawn again, to a bend where a lane leaves it to the east. Both sides are lined with lots holding frame dwellings, sheds, a smoke house and a wagon or auto house; house numbers run from 101 down to 82 on the west side (block 219) and 131 down to 82 on the east (block 218). The street is about 32 to 33 feet wide. The margins are marked no exposure, and a north arrow is drawn at the lower right.
notes: South Main is today's South Main Street; the Lane at the bend has no named counterpart in OpenStreetMap.
The modern South Main Street bends more sharply here than the drawn street.
Placed from two building and lot corners carried from part 1 of this sheet, which draws the same lot; low confidence.

sheet-3-1.description: The main map of Sheet 3 shows the north part of Stewartsville around the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, at 100 feet to an inch. North is drawn straight up, but the fit puts true north about 12 degrees clockwise. Across the top runs Morris Avenue or Morris Turnpike with scattered dwellings, a garage and poultry houses. Below it lies a small grid of residential streets: Hulshizer Avenue, Edison Avenue and Prospect (Railroad Avenue), crossed by Palmer, Thompson and Beacon, with Rodney, Cherry Alley, Spruce Alley and two Cedar Alleys between the blocks, built up with frame dwellings on narrow lots. North Main Street crosses the sheet diagonally from upper left to lower right. The railroad runs along Railroad Avenue with the passenger station, a freight house and section house, and a siding. South of the tracks Depot runs down to North Main Street past a few dwellings, and the dry bed of the former Morris Canal crosses at the lower right. Mellick's Brook flows north at the right edge under the railroad, beside a road. The upper left and lower left corners hold two insets of works on the Morris Turnpike.
notes: Morris Avenue or Morris Turnpike is today's NJ 57; Prospect (Railroad Avenue) is Prospect Street; Depot is Warren Street, which today meets North Main Street at Thomas Stewart Way about 39 m north-west of the drawn canal crossing.
Rodney, Cedar Alley and Spruce Alley survive as service roads (Rodney Street, Cedar Alley, Spruce Alley).
The north arrow points straight up although the fit gives north about 12 degrees clockwise.
Beacon Street / NJ 57 and Depot / North Main were left out of the fit (widened road; junction moved).

Scale 100 ft. Part 1: Morris Av. or Morris Turnpike (NJ 57), Hulshizer, Palmer, Thompson, Beacon, Edison, Prospect (Railroad Av.), Depot (Warren Street), N. Main, D. L. & W. R. R. depot. North arrow drawn straight up but the fit gives north 12 degrees clockwise. Part 2 (inset, top left): Dowling and Son coal yard, Morris Turnpike at Road (Richline Hill Road). Part 3 (inset, bottom left): S. A. Shillinger feed mill, Morris Turnpike at Montana Rd. (Lows Hollow Road).

sheet-3-2.description: This inset at the upper left of Sheet 3 shows the Dowling and Son coal yard and general store (M. E. Dowling, owner of buildings) on the south side of the Morris Turnpike, at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow. The turnpike crosses the top of the inset, 35 to 40 feet wide. A 20 foot road runs south from it at the left edge, crossing the dry bed of the former Morris Canal, which runs along the bottom of the inset. Between them are a dwelling, a coal pocket, scales and a store and dwelling, with a note that farm barns lie about 300 feet away. Text notes that the owners live on the premises and there is no fire apparatus. The margins are marked no exposure.
notes: Morris Turnpike is today's NJ 57; the Road is taken to be Richline Hill Road, whose modern line runs about 20 degrees off the drawn road.
Placed from one hand-picked junction with the atlas scale and a north of 41 degrees from the drawn turnpike; low confidence.

sheet-3-3.description: This inset at the lower left of Sheet 3 shows the S. A. Shillinger feed mill and coal yard on the north side of the Morris Turnpike, at 100 feet to an inch with a north arrow pointing up. The turnpike runs along the bottom of the inset. Montana Road, 20 feet wide, leaves it northward between Mellick's Brook on the west and a mill pond on the east, with the mill building, coal pockets, scales and a penstock beside it. Notes record no watchman, power by water, a stove in the office, electric light and no fire apparatus. West of the mill are a few lots with frame dwellings and sheds along the turnpike, numbered 401 to 405, and east of the pond more dwellings, a barn and a wagon house numbered 408 to 410. The land south of the turnpike is marked vacant. The scale bar of the sheet is drawn at the bottom right of the inset.
notes: Morris Turnpike is today's NJ 57; Montana Road is today's Lows Hollow Road, whose line and fork at the turnpike match the drawing.
Placed from one hand-picked junction with the atlas scale and a north of 22 degrees fitted to both roads and the parcels; low to medium confidence.
